parsed.explanation: The dossier documents state-directed targeting of trans people at the top of the precedence ladder: a 2024 morality law imposing a preventive surveillance duty over homosexuality and lesbianism, a penal code with a religious-law clause permitting death for same-sex activity, and security services systematically pursuing gay men and trans women with arbitrary detention, sexual violence, flogging and public confirmation of punishments. Trans people are explicitly identified as facing gravest risk, including exploitation and violence. No protection, remedy or rule-of-law recourse exists; the ICC prosecutor's 2025 warrant request corroborates persecution of the LGBTQ community as crimes against humanity. Rule 13 requires extrapolation to the risk these structural facts imply, not to a midpoint.

entry_documents.interaction: Dossier states entry/visa and marker policy unresolved; cannot assume any mitigating border practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Security officials systematically pursue trans women; arbitrary detention, physical and sexual assault in custody, flogging confirmed by supreme court social media; no trans-prisoner placement practice documented but no protection either.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Morality-law surveillance duty feeds directly into detention; leaked personal data used by movement members to pursue individuals.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facilities law not documented; virtue-police enforcement nationwide with no provincial breakdown.

care_services.exposure: No legal protection on gender identity; health services historically inaccessible to LGBTI people; condom distribution restricted; care denial when trans status known is a credible risk in a collapsing-protection environment.
care_services.interaction: Detection through any health encounter risks onward exposure to authorities.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing is explicit and codified: morality law criminalising homosexuality even between spouses; religious-law clause permitting death penalty; floggings nearly doubled to 1,110 in 2025; trans women named gravest-risk group; street attacks on men read as gay.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Religious-authority enforcement dominates; ICC prosecutor requested arrest warrants for LGBTQ persecution.

minors_guardians.exposure: Article 430 can reach any adult assisting a minor; Article 427 increases penalties; vigilante honour killings for homosexuality carry lesser punishment (Article 398); bacha bazi history of trafficking and abuse of boys with police complicity. An adult travelling with a minor faces state and vigilante exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Caregiving or partnership with a minor is itself prosecutable exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented street attacks on men read as gay; movement members and supporters attacking, threatening and expelling LGBT people from homes; family and neighbour abuse surged after takeover; perpetrators face impunity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None; police complicity in historic abuses; no hate-crime recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Non-reporting assumption makes travellers soft targets for extortion and violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No protection exists on sexual orientation or gender identity before or after 2021 takeover; courts defer to religious authorities; consular or appeal pathways absent from record; blacklisting and data leaks used against targets.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No functioning remedy at any stage; unknowns (border practice, provincial variation) resolve adversely under rule 13.

anchor_checks.comparison: Direct parallel: religious-authority morality enforcement, death-penalty exposure for gender/sexual transgression, documented flogging and custody abuse, no independent remedy. This dossier lacks the documented execution of a trans visitor, but custody sexual violence, escalating flogging and systematic pursuit of trans women sit at the same tier.

0.15-A involves pretrial custody with beatings and illusory remedies; this jurisdiction is materially worse: state-directed morality surveillance, death-penalty clause, ICC-level persecution finding, and trans women explicitly identified as gravest-risk. Rates below 0.15-A.

0.25-D has selective enforcement, entrapment and short detention with appellate restraint; here enforcement is nationwide, escalating, and punishments include flogging with supreme-court endorsement and no functioning appeal. Substantially below 0.25-D.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a state-directed campaign: morality-law surveillance, systematic pursuit of trans women by security officials, documented custody sexual violence, flogging with public endorsement, and a religious-law death-penalty clause, with zero protective machinery at any level. Severity is tier 1-2 on the precedence ladder and frequency is high and escalating (floggings nearly doubled in 2025). Uncertainty about border and facilities practice cannot soften a record in which every documented stage — surveillance, detention, custody, street exposure — is hostile. Structural facts (criminalisation, death penalty, no recognition, no recourse, ICC-documented persecution) extrapolate to near the 0.05 tier, slightly above it only because visitor-specific executions are not individually documented.
